title: Conversation Memory Compaction - Arch Review Notes
body:
Meeting: Conversation Memory Compaction - architecture review
Date: 2025-10-21 11:00-12:15 PT
Location: Zoom / #eng-serving-runtime
Facilitator: Priya Natarajan
Attendees: Priya N., Ethan M., Leila C., Marco R., Samira P., Jonah K., (notes by Priya)

Context / problem statement:
We need a service-side approach to bound per-conversation memory usage for long-running, multiparty conversations that accumulate KV-cache, embeddings, and local session state. Customers (hosted + dedicated + private) are spinning up hour+ conversations where user messages + tool outputs + multi-turn embeddings push memory per-session into GBs. Left unchecked this increases SLO risk (OOMs), degrades tail latency, and makes predictable capacity planning almost impossible for Dedicated pools. The goal of today’s review: align on an architecture for "conversation memory compaction" that is safe, observable, and rollable, while preserving quality for common workloads.

Agenda:
- Walk through current telemetry (Leila)
- Proposed compaction model (Marco)
- Alternatives considered (Samira)
- Compatibility with Private deploys and KMS (Jonah)
- Rollout and canary metrics (Ethan)
- Actions and owner assignments

Telemetry snapshot (Leila):
- 90th/99th token memory per session has increased ~35% QoQ on hosted clusters; top 5% of sessions account for ~48% of active KV memory.
- Median conversation length by tokens: 1.2k; top 1% exceed 40k tokens.
- OOM incidents in prod nodes correlate with multi-session colocations from 3 customers on same Dedicated pool (ticket: PROD-4123).
- Suggested signals: per-session kv_bytes, embedding_store_bytes, last_read_turn_ts, and per-session cache_hit_rate.

Proposed architecture (Marco) — "tiered compaction" model:
- Soft limit + adaptive compaction: each session has a soft-memory ceiling (configurable per-tenant). When soft limit exceeded, perform lightweight compaction steps incrementally rather than immediate hard eviction.
- Compaction steps (ordered, incremental):
  1) Prefix trimming (drop oldest non-critical message tokens from prefix cache up to X% or by token budget).
  2) Embedding checkpointing: offload older embeddings to persistent per-tenant cold store (S3/GCS) with LRU index and lazy rehydration on access.
  3) Summarization pass: run a short, cheap summarizer model (or use cached user-provided summary) to compress earlier turns into a single special-turn token with metadata.
  4) Hard eviction as last resort: drop conversational KV entries per-config (policy: oldest-first or semantic least-recently-used).
- Each step emits events to tracing and increments a compaction counter for decision visibility.
- Policy is tenant-configurable: default soft ceiling = 500MB session, soft-to-hard grace = 3 compaction cycles, ability to pin sessions (no compaction) for high-SLA customers.

Rationale / tradeoffs discussed:
- Prefers incremental/lightweight ops to avoid large latency spikes during requests.
- Offloading embeddings to cold store reduces RAM but adds a small rehydration latency on rare hits; acceptable for >60d history items.
- Summarization introduces risk of lost fidelity. To mitigate, we keep original content in cold store for a configurable retention window (default 30 days) and surface a human-readable "compression confidence" metric.
- For private deployments on air-gapped networks, embedding offload must be optional. We must support a mode where compacted items are kept on local disk with encryption via customer KMS.

Alternatives considered (Samira):
- Aggressive TTL-only approach: set a fixed TTL for all conversation state. Pros: simple. Cons: poor UX for long-running sessions and breaks recall-based features.
- Strict per-session hard limits enforced on write: reject new messages when limit hit. Pros: predictable capacity. Cons: high error rate for customers and poor product experience.
- Per-token micro-pricing with auto-eviction incentive: monetize long sessions and evict on non-payment. Discussed but out-of-scope for current infra change — requires billing + UX work.

Compatibility notes (Jonah):
- Private deployments must be able to opt-out of remote cold offload and instead write to local object cache. Add two config flags: compact.offload.enabled (bool) and compact.offload.type (s3|gcs|local).
- All offloaded blobs must be encrypted with tenant KMS. For managed hosted customers we use Redwood KMS; for Private we must integrate with customer KMS/HSM via existing KMS connectors.
- Summarizer must be a model variant selectable per-tenant and should run in a rate-limited pool so it doesn't affect primary LLM serving concurrency.

Observability / SLOs (Ethan):
- Expose metrics: session_compaction_count{reason}, session_compaction_stage, per_session_kv_bytes, session_compression_confidence.
- New dashboard for "compaction health" and per-tenant memory pressure heatmap.
- Canary success criteria: no increase >2% in p95 token latency for canary traffic, compaction events logged, and <1% increase in rehydration tail latency.

Operational rollout plan:
- Phase 0 (dev): implement compaction pipeline + unit tests + local integration (2 sprints).
- Phase 1 (internal canary): enable for internal tenants only, synthetic load tests, enable detailed tracing (1 sprint).
- Phase 2 (hosted soft canary): opt-in for low-risk hosted tenants, track metrics for 2 weeks.
- Phase 3 (general enablement): default-on for hosted, opt-out for private until configuration validated. Dedicated pools get soft limit defaults lowered and controls surfaced in Console.
- Feature flags: compact.v1.enabled (bool), compact.v1.offload-mode (enum), compact.v1.summarizer-model (string).

Decisions made:
- Adopt tiered compaction model with incremental steps (prefix trim, offload, summarization, hard eviction).
- Default soft ceiling 500MB; implement tenant override via Console + API.
- Require encryption for any offloaded artifacts; Private deployments default to local mode.
- Summarization is implemented as an optional stage; default enabled but configurable per-tenant.

Open questions / unresolved:
- How long should cold-store retention be before permanent deletion? (default 30d proposed) — ACTION: decide retention policy with Legal/Privacy. (owner: Samira, due: 2025-10-28)
- Cost model for cold-store rehydration IO — need finance input to understand unit economics for hosted vs dedicated tenants. (owner: Leila, due: 2025-10-28)
- Summarizer Fallback: if summarizer fails, do we continue to offload raw items or pause compaction? (owner: Marco to propose logic, due: 2025-10-27)

Action items (owner / due):
- Marco: Draft PR for compaction pipeline module + proto API for session compaction events. (PR target: runtime repo, due: 2025-10-30)
- Leila: Add telemetry collection for session_compaction_stage and compile baseline dashboards. (due: 2025-10-27)
- Jonah: Update Private deploy docs with offload config flags and KMS integration checklist. (due: 2025-10-29)
- Ethan: Define Canary acceptance dashboard and create Alert runbook for compaction regressions. (due: 2025-10-28)
- Samira: Engage Legal on cold-store retention policy and prepare privacy impact note. (due: 2025-10-28)
- Priya: Coordinate canary tenant list and create Console UI mocks for tenant memory override. (due: 2025-10-24)

Next steps / follow up:
- Weekly sync (Wednesdays 9am PT) to track progress until Phase 1 complete.
- Marco will post initial PR and link to this doc in the PR description.
- Revisit decision after internal canary results (scheduled review 2025-11-12).

Appendix / references:
- Related tickets: PROD-4123, INF-2031 (compaction metrics schema)
- GH PR reference: runtime#1987 (prototype compaction pipeline)
- Confluence: Conversation Snapshotting Design (linked above)

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a working doc; expect changes as PRs land. Add comments inline or drop notes in #eng-serving-runtime. If you have strong objections to summarization as a compaction step, flag ASAP — we need to finalize approach before design freeze next sprint.

End of notes.
